cards.power: Play this to instantly discard the "Official Narrative" card from play.
cards.lore: Uncle FrizzleBob's epistemic sabotage expansion! No humans, no neutrality, just pure analog financial wrestling! Style: Pulp conspiracy poster. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit tearing a dollar bill in half. Mood: Furious glee.

cards.power: Force your opponent to reveal their hand. Steal all cards with a 'Profit' value.
cards.lore: "It determines how we proceed with our investigation. 9/11 was a crime, and detectives must identify the perpetrators." Style: Noir detective illustration. Subject: Bloodhound in trenchcoat sniffing a trail of gold coins. Mood: Relentless certainty.

cards.power: Negate any systemic anomaly by declaring it a "random fluke."
cards.lore: "This would be one of the most extraordinary coincidences in the history of mankind if it was a coincidence." Style: Retro industrial. Subject: Absurd Rube Goldberg machine labeled COINCIDENCE GENERATOR. Mood: Dry bureaucratic menace.

cards.power: Nullify any investigation card.
cards.lore: "You got to go through 10 veils before you get to the real Source, thanks to the Secretary of the Treasury." Style: Ornate bureaucratic theatre. Subject: Peacock in suit standing behind ten translucent curtains. Mood: Smug obstruction.

cards.power: Control the board's highest value asset for a fraction of the cost.
cards.lore: In 1998, the Port Authority agreed to privatize the WTC. By July 2001, a 99-year lease was signed for $3.2B. Style: Corporate propaganda poster. Subject: Frog in hard hat planting a SOLD sign on two giant towers. Mood: Triumphant greed.

cards.power: Leverage 0.4% of your own assets to control a multi-billion dollar empire.
cards.lore: Other players only put down $14 million of their own money, financed by GMAC and individual investors. Style: Wall Street grotesque. Subject: Fat pig in suit balancing a $3.2B gold bar on a $14 matchstick. Mood: Obscene leverage.

cards.power: Double your coverage right before a disaster. If disaster strikes, claim it happened twice.
cards.lore: The leaseholder insisted on doubling the insurance to $3.55B, demanding courts construe the attacks as two separate events to win $7.1B. Style: Crooked insurance ad. Subject: Squirrel in suit pointing at two identical fire claims. Mood: Cheerful fraud.

cards.power: Get your initial equity refunded while maintaining total control of the site.
cards.lore: In a secret 2003 deal, the Port Authority paid back 80% of the initial equity. Profit: $4.55 billion and counting. Style: Back-alley deal illustration. Subject: Two reptiles exchanging a briefcase under a streetlight. Mood: Conspiratorial satisfaction.

cards.power: Host the most sensitive data on the exact floors of an impending impact.
cards.lore: Marsh & McLennan occupied the exact impact zone of the North Tower, housing 2,000 employees and critical transaction data. Style: Architectural blueprint. Subject: Bear hunched over floor plans with impact zone circled in red. Mood: Cold precision.

cards.power: Execute massive paperless transactions unseen by any other commercial entity on the planet.
cards.lore: Marsh was the first financial company on the planet to employ this specific type of paperless transaction technology. Style: Retro-tech thriller. Subject: Raccoon vanishing behind a waterfall of digital zeros. Mood: Untraceable velocity.

cards.power: Generate phantom purchase orders. If confronted, urge the Feds to look in your own business.
cards.lore: Severe fiscal anomalies and unnecessary hardware sales led investigators to the heart of the Marsh.com mystery. Style: Forensic accounting noir. Subject: Fox surrounded by floating receipts stamped VOID. Mood: Gleeful misdirection.

cards.power: Schedule an all-hands meeting in a doomed building, but dial in from home.
cards.lore: The executive who buried the anomaly inquiry was safe at home, while the IT staff investigating the fraud perished in the conference call. Style: Dark domestic satire. Subject: Smug bear on couch with phone, skyscrapers burning through window. Mood: Comfortable distance.

cards.power: Retrieve impossible data from ground zero. Refuse to ever speak of it again.
cards.lore: The German firm recovered data showing a massive, unexplained surge in transactions prior to the attacks. Now? "I could not give you any additional information." Style: Spy thriller tech lab. Subject: Crow in lab coat extracting a smoking hard drive from rubble, mouth sealed shut. Mood: Institutional silence.

cards.power: Co-opt mainframe computers externally during a crisis to purge data.
cards.lore: Right before and during the attacks, Deutsche Bank computers were externally taken over for a massive data download and purge. Style: Hacker thriller. Subject: Shadowy wolf's hands at keyboard, clock showing 40 minutes, data deleting on screen. Mood: Surgical urgency.

cards.power: Mask illicit mega-trades as random market fluctuations.
cards.lore: "It could turn out that Americans went on an absolute shopping binge on that Tuesday morning." — Convar Director, dripping with irony. Style: Satirical consumer culture. Subject: Sheep in suits stampeding into a stock exchange labeled MALL. Mood: Willful absurdity.

cards.power: Establish the Official Enemy within 2 hours of an event, deflecting all financial inquiries.
cards.lore: Marsh's Chief of Risk Management wasn't in his doomed office; he was on NBC blaming Bin Laden before the dust settled. Style: Breaking news grotesque. Subject: Fox in suit at TV anchor desk pointing at a target while buildings burn behind him. Mood: Shameless opportunism.

cards.power: Turn a $180K bet into $2.4 million in a single day.
cards.lore: More than 2,000 contracts betting against United and American Airlines — 30 times the normal volume. "Horrific, evil insider trading." Style: Wall Street casino. Subject: Coyote in pinstripe suit raking chips from a crashed airline model. Mood: Audacious avarice.

cards.power: Buy calls on defense contractors right before a 20-year war starts.
cards.lore: A six-fold increase in call options for Raytheon allowed traders to cash in when the military deployed missiles to Afghanistan. Style: Military-industrial infomercial. Subject: Eagle in suit holding Raytheon stock ticker next to exploding rocket. Mood: Premeditated profit.

cards.power: Launch global probes that mysteriously fizzle out when they hit US soil.
cards.lore: Foreign finance ministers were certain: "People connected to the terrorists must have been trying to profit from this tragedy." Style: Spy thriller map room. Subject: Bloodhound following money trail that disappears at US border. Mood: Deliberate incompetence.

cards.power: Destroy all potentially responsive records regarding options trading.
cards.lore: When FOIA researchers asked for the documentary evidence of the pre-9/11 options trading, they were told the records were destroyed. Style: Office horror. Subject: Rat in uniform feeding documents into shredder labeled EVIDENCE. Mood: Bureaucratic obliteration.

cards.power: Double your stock value on airport security systems. Ignore all FBI interviews.
cards.lore: Wirt D. Walker III bought 56,000 shares of Stratex. The FBI never interviewed him because he had "no ties to terrorism." Style: Corporate scandal illustration. Subject: Hawk in blazer staring smugly at a soaring stock chart next to airport scanners. Mood: Untouchable privilege.

cards.power: Host the enemy's family for a private equity breakfast on the day of the attack.
cards.lore: The Carlyle Group was meeting in DC with the brother of Osama Bin Laden on the morning of September 11th. Style: Luxury horror. Subject: Vultures in suits at white-tablecloth breakfast, TV showing smoking towers in background. Mood: Untroubled affluence.

cards.power: Route criminal trades through the former firm of the CIA's Executive Director.
cards.lore: The unusual 2,500 contract put order was brokered by the firm formerly chaired by the current #3 man at the CIA. Style: Spy noir. Subject: Owl in CIA badge handing a trade slip through a revolving door labeled AB Brown. Mood: Institutional impunity.

cards.power: Possess perfect foresight. Remain uninvestigated forever.
cards.lore: Former CIA agent Robert Baer admitted on video knowing a DOD staffer who cashed out the day before. No agency ever investigated him. Style: Beach noir. Subject: Iguana in sunglasses counting cash by the ocean, San Diego skyline behind him. Mood: Prophetic ease.

cards.power: Examine 9.5 million transactions and conclude nothing happened.
cards.lore: They didn't say insider trading didn't happen. They said "those who had advanced knowledge didn't trade." Begging the question: WHO had knowledge? Style: Official absurdism. Subject: Blind horse in SEC uniform stamping CLEARED on a mountain of documents. Mood: Procedural blindness.

cards.power: Place 95% of the put options on an airline and get a free pass.
cards.lore: The 9/11 Commission dismissed the trades because the US-based investor had "no conceivable ties to Al-Qaeda." Style: Commission hearing grotesque. Subject: Pig at witness stand shrugging while 95% bar chart floats behind it. Mood: Teflon confidence.

cards.power: Prove beyond a statistical doubt that insiders traded. Get completely ignored by the government.
cards.lore: Three separate scientific papers concluded with high probability that the anomalous trading was the result of advanced knowledge. Style: Academic tragedy. Subject: Owl professor presenting statistical graphs to completely empty government hearing chairs. Mood: Righteous futility.

cards.power: Declare the origin of the money "of little practical significance."
cards.lore: The final word of the US Government rejected the first rule of criminal investigation: Follow the Money. Style: Official ceremony satire. Subject: Pelican in suit waving away a mountain of dollar bills with one flip of the wing. Mood: Authoritative indifference.

cards.power: Map and monitor a target's entire system and personnel in real time.
cards.lore: The ultimate risk management software. The person running it has a God's eye view to foresee problems—or cause them. Style: Surveillance tech horror. Subject: Giant eye inside a web of government building blueprints. Mood: Omniscient calm.

cards.power: Merge risk management and enterprise architecture to prevent—or execute—massive failures.
cards.lore: JP Morgan sought software to stop rogue trading and massive computer failures. Ptech was the industry guru recommendation. Style: Corporate thriller diagram. Subject: Gecko in boardroom unveiling blueprints labeled both SHIELD and SWORD. Mood: Dual-use menace.

cards.cardName: The Keys to the Cyber Kingdom
cards.power: Gain top-level security clearance to the most protected servers in the world.
cards.lore: Ptech built detailed pictures of agency vulnerabilities, showing exactly how they could be exploited by those of ill intent. Style: Heist thriller. Subject: Wolf in developer hoodie holding a giant keyring with IRS, FBI, NATO, White House labels. Mood: Quiet omnipotence.

cards.power: Find the exact holes in the defense escalation process.
cards.lore: Ptech worked in the FAA basement, specifically looking for holes in how agencies respond to a hijacking emergency. Style: Technical thriller. Subject: Raccoons in FAA basement mapping hijacking response gaps on a whiteboard. Mood: Methodical infiltration.

cards.power: Seize $1.4M in terror funds, then get permanently blocked by your own bosses.
cards.lore: Agents Wright and Vincent were thwarted from opening a criminal investigation into the very man financing Ptech. Style: Institutional tragedy. Subject: Two bloodhounds straining at leashes held by their own police chief. Mood: Institutional sabotage.

cards.power: Boast of ties to the Vice President while funding startups and terror simultaneously.
cards.lore: The multi-millionaire angel investor behind Ptech was later put on a US Treasury terrorist watch list. Style: Society portrait gone wrong. Subject: Leopard in tux shaking hands with VP while signing terror check behind his back. Mood: Brazen duality.

cards.power: Provide $5 million in seed capital to infiltrate the US government.
cards.lore: The investment firm backed by al-Qadi that got Ptech off the ground. Style: Corporate cover art. Subject: Scorpion signing a venture capital check labeled PTECH in a glass-walled boardroom. Mood: Laundered legitimacy.

cards.power: Create a financial facade to conceal terror support.
cards.lore: Shared office space with al-Qadi, provided founding loans for Ptech, and was run by Ptech's own Chief Scientist. Style: Shell company diagram. Subject: Horse in hardhat holding For Lease sign over a building with three secret doors. Mood: Layered concealment.

cards.power: Write software for the government by day, praise holy war by night.
cards.lore: Ptech's Chief Architect quoted Bin Laden's mentor while mapping the operational blueprints of the US military. Style: Split-screen identity portrait. Subject: Wolf at computer coding, half in government badge half in shadow. Mood: Double life as daily routine.

cards.power: Delay a federal raid by two weeks to ensure all evidence is gone.
cards.lore: When the FBI finally raided Ptech in 2002, the company was given two weeks advanced warning. Style: Spy comedy. Subject: Turtle mailman delivering RAID SCHEDULED letter to office with two-week countdown calendar. Mood: Absurd complicity.

cards.power: Declare an infiltrated system perfectly safe the day after a raid.
cards.lore: Ridge declared that Ptech "in no way jeopardizes the security of the country." Style: Bureaucratic satire. Subject: Bulldog in Homeland Security uniform stamping FINE on a smoking server rack. Mood: Institutional damage control.

cards.power: Co-chair an investigation while ignoring your own financial ties.
cards.lore: Kean had a $24M real estate transaction with BMI. The Commission never looked into Ptech. Style: Official portrait corruption. Subject: Swan in suit chairing hearing while stuffing BMI paperwork into briefcase. Mood: Genteel self-dealing.

cards.power: Declare war on your own bureaucracy 24 hours before a catastrophe.
cards.lore: "The adversary is closer to home... It's the Pentagon bureaucracy." Style: Martial press conference. Subject: Eagle at podium pointing accusingly at Pentagon building, calendar shows Sept 10. Mood: Preemptive misdirection.

cards.power: Fudge entries, process without documentation, or make them up entirely.
cards.lore: In 1999 alone, $2.3 trillion in transactions could not be properly accounted for, $8,000 for every citizen in America. Style: Pentagon accounting horror. Subject: Bear pushing stacks of cash under a rug labeled RECONCILED. Mood: Industrial-scale nonchalance.

cards.power: Reassign anyone who cares about doing a good job.
cards.lore: Jim Minnery tried to track down $300 million. His director asked him, "Why do you care about this stuff?" Style: Office satire. Subject: Manager shrugging at accountant holding $300M receipt, reassignment form already in hand. Mood: Institutional apathy as policy.

cards.power: Fail to untangle the financial snarl, but get a massive defense budget anyway.
cards.lore: Tasked with solving the $2.3 trillion missing money, Zakheim instead drafted papers calling for military transformation. Style: Bureaucratic ladder climbing. Subject: Octopus with ledger full of question marks signing Pentagon budget increase. Mood: Failing upward at scale.

cards.power: Develop remote control systems for airborne vehicles, then market them to the Pentagon.
cards.lore: Zakheim's former company provided advanced military electronics and remote flight tech to DARPA prior to 9/11. Style: Cold war tech thriller. Subject: Owl engineer holding remote control with paper plane labeled DARPA looping in background. Mood: Plausible deniability.

cards.power: Write a white paper predicting exactly what you need to conquer the world.
cards.lore: PNAC called for a sweeping transformation of the military, including biological warfare targeting specific genotypes. Style: Think tank thriller. Subject: Lions in suits presenting a world map with color-coded invasion zones. Mood: Academic menace.

cards.power: Receive a catastrophic and catalyzing event exactly when your political agenda requires it.
cards.lore: "The process of transformation... is likely to be a long one, absent some catastrophic and catalyzing event." Style: Document thriller. Subject: Hand circling catastrophic and catalyzing event in a classified document. Calendar shows Sept 2001. Mood: Prophetic planning.

cards.power: Use a crisis to bypass all political opposition to a $50 billion budget increase.
cards.lore: "We know that the thing that tends to register on people is fear... we've got to be smarter than that." Style: Political horror campaign. Subject: Deer-in-headlights citizens herded toward a $50B budget approval stamp. Mood: Engineered panic.

cards.power: Concentrate your entire financial auditing team in a single, newly renovated target zone.
cards.lore: The office of Resource Services Washington had just moved back into Wedge 1. 34 bookkeepers and budget analysts were killed. Style: Floor plan horror. Subject: Blueprint of Pentagon Wedge 1 with all accounting offices circled in red. Mood: Architectural precision meets tragedy.

cards.power: Lose the personnel required to ever figure out where the missing trillions went.
cards.lore: The Army was unable to produce a financial report for 2001 due to the loss of accountants in the attack. Style: Government tragedy. Subject: Empty accountant desks with unfinished balance sheets, Pentagon smoke outside window. Mood: Permanent incompleteness.

cards.power: Hire the masterminds of corporate accounting fraud to run the military's budget.
cards.lore: Before becoming Secretary of the Army, White was a senior executive at Enron, the largest accounting fraud in history. Style: Rogues gallery portrait. Subject: Fox in Army uniform with Enron logo pin on lapel, reviewing Pentagon ledgers. Mood: Revolving door confidence.

cards.power: Destroy 3,000 to 4,000 documents on active corporate fraud investigations.
cards.lore: The SEC occupied floors 11-13 of WTC Building 7, wiping out evidence on Enron and others when it collapsed. Style: Evidence room noir. Subject: Filing cabinets labeled ENRON INVESTIGATION tumbling into rubble, Building 7 collapsing behind. Mood: Convenient catastrophe.

cards.power: Inflate the unaccountable money from $2.3T to $8.5T over a decade without a single Congressional hearing.
cards.lore: Rumsfeld's war on the Pentagon bureaucracy was highly successful at losing even more money. Style: Congressional absurdism. Subject: Bear rolling a snowball labeled $2.3T down a hill, it becomes $8.5T at the bottom. Mood: Effortless scale.

cards.power: Doctor books to hide missing money using standard operating procedure.
cards.lore: If money is missing at the end of the day, just input a false number to cover it up and submit a balanced budget. Style: Office procedural horror. Subject: Mouse at Pentagon terminal changing $2.3T to $0.00, boss approving with a stamp. Mood: Bureaucratic corruption as routine.

cards.power: Spend 15 years falsifying financial records for the Navy.
cards.lore: "Money was missing from the report every month." Style: Long-con portrait. Subject: Raccoon at desk surrounded by 15 years of Navy ledgers, eraser worn to a nub. Mood: Exhausted complicity.

cards.power: Completely lose $6 billion in cash in a war zone.
cards.lore: The US wasted $50 billion and completely lost $6 billion in Iraq. That's more than most countries spend on their entire defense in a year. Style: Desert war comedy. Subject: Camel standing next to a crater labeled $6B shrugging at a US general. Mood: Weaponized incompetence.

cards.power: Combine Insurance, Insider Trading, and Military Fraud to win the pot.
cards.lore: Insurance scams, financial fraud, missing money, and evidence destroyed. $8.5 trillion remains to investigate. Style: Final boss splash art. Subject: Three-headed lizard in suit holding insurance policy, stock ticker, and Pentagon budget. Mood: Total systemic control.

cards.power: Ask the perpetrators to investigate themselves.
cards.lore: The answers to 9/11 are not going to come from the suspects of the crime. Style: Commission theatre. Subject: Fox presiding over hearing table with all other seats also filled by foxes. Mood: Closed-loop justice.

cards.power: Ensure that potentially responsive records are always "destroyed."
cards.lore: From CBOE to Convar, the evidence of the money trail always manages to disappear into the ether. Style: Evidence trail vanishing act. Subject: Paper trail from CBOE to Convar, each document bursting into smoke. Mood: Systemic erasure.

cards.power: Discard all illusions. Game over.
cards.lore: "They told you 9/11 changed everything. They were right: it made the house infinitely rich. Follow the Kayfabe-Money, kids!" Style: Final panel splash. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit MC standing on a pile of gold coins, pointing at the camera. Mood: Vindicated fury.
